reason: The support needs a stable footing, so clearing and preparing the ground with the excavator is a sensible first step.
expectation: The excavator will prepare the ground for the replacement support.

effect: The excavator exposed firm ground for the new footing without disturbing the loaded cribbing.
reaction: The precaution around the existing support makes sense.
reason: Steel on the prepared ground is a plausible way to make the broad footing and support.
expectation: The steel will form a footing or frame for the replacement support.

effect: The replacement support is built on a broad footing and matches the sound lower-stage joints; it now needs to be fitted to the lander.
reaction: The layered footing and braced frame make the load path clear.
reason: The new support matches the lander's surviving joints, so fitting it to the tilted lander is the natural next step.
expectation: The replacement support will be fitted and the lander brought level.

effect: The replacement support was fitted and took the lander's weight, completing the level launch platform.
reaction: The straight ladder was a satisfying visible sign of the repair.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building and fitting the replacement support was worthwhile: the broad footing, bracing and careful transfer of weight made the repair physically understandable.

leastWorthwhile.text: Clearing the ground was a straightforward preparatory step, though the precaution of leaving the loaded cribbing undisturbed gave it a purpose.

surprise.text: The replacement leg stays on Mars when the upper cabin lifts away; I had not expected the support's role to end there.

arbitrary.text: No action felt especially arbitrary; each contributed clearly to preparing, building or fitting the support.

continue.text: I would continue to see the departure and the samples' journey home. This chapter made the repair feel consequential, though its combinations were fairly predictable.
